title: Eventual injectivity of residue-tensor comparisons in local algebra approximations
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set. For each $i\in I$ let $\varphi_i:R_i\to S_i$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be another such homomorphism. Here local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. For $i\le j$ let $r_{ji}:R_i\to R_j$ and $s_{ji}:S_i\to S_j$ be local homomorphisms, with local cocone maps $r_i:R_i\to R$ and $s_i:S_i\to S$. All ring squares commute, transitions are identities at equal indices and respect composition, and the cocones are compatible. Suppose $R=\varinjlim R_i$ and $S=\varinjlim S_i$ as rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. These colimits are algebraic: elements come from stages and equality is detected at a common later stage. Put $\mathfrak m_i=\mathfrak m_{R_i}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$, $k_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$, and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Let $M_i$ be finite $S_i$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with additive transitions $m_{ji}$ semilinear over $s_{ji}$, and let $M$ be an $S$-module with additive cocone maps $\mu_i:M_i\to M$ semilinear over $s_i$. The module transitions and cocone obey the identity, composition and compatibility laws. Suppose $M=\varinjlim M_i$ as abelian groups, with its induced $S$-action. For $i\le j$ suppose the canonical map $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$, $a\otimes b\mapsto s_{ji}(a)\varphi_j(b)$, is a localization at a multiplicative subset $W_{ji}$, and the canonical map $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to M_j$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a m_{ji}(x)$, is an isomorphism. A localization at $W$ means that elements of $W$ become units, every target element is a fraction with denominator in $W$, and an element of the source mapping to zero is killed by some element of $W$. Tensor products have their usual universal bilinear meaning [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. All sets and objects are placed in one common sufficiently large universe. Assume each $S_i$ is essentially of finite type over $R_i$, that is, a localization of a finite type $R_i$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Set $D_i=S_i\otimes_{R_i}k$, $P_i=M_i\otimes_{R_i}k$, and $P=M\otimes_Rk$, using $r_i$ for the $R_i$-action on $k$. Let $d_{ji}:D_i\to D_j$ and $p_{ji}:P_i\to P_j$ send $a\otimes c$ to $s_{ji}(a)\otimes c$ and $x\otimes c$ to $m_{ji}(x)\otimes c$. Give $P$ its natural compatible $D_i$-actions and let $\Psi_i:P_i\to P$ send $x\otimes c$ to $\mu_i(x)\otimes c$. Then $D_i$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $P_i$ and $\ker\Psi_i$ are finite over $D_i$, and the maps $D_i\to(S_i/\mathfrak m_iS_i)\otimes_{k_i}k$, $a\otimes c\mapsto[a]\otimes c$, $P_i\to(M_i/\mathfrak m_iM_i)\otimes_{k_i}k$, $x\otimes c\mapsto[x]\otimes c$, and $P\to M/\mathfrak mM$, $x\otimes[r]\mapsto[rx]$, are well defined isomorphisms. Under the last two, $\Psi_i$ corresponds to the map $(M_i/\mathfrak m_iM_i)\otimes_{k_i}k\to M/\mathfrak mM$, $[x]\otimes[r]\mapsto[r\mu_i(x)]$. For each $i\le j$, $d_{ji}$ exhibits $D_j$ as the localization of $D_i$ at the image of $W_{ji}$ under $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to D_i$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes\overline{r_j(b)}$, and $p_{ji}$ exhibits $P_j$ as the corresponding module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The maps $\Psi_i$ exhibit $P$ as the colimit of the underlying abelian groups $P_i$. For every $i_0\in I$ there is $i_1\ge i_0$ such that $\Psi_j$ is injective for every $j\ge i_1$.

proof.text: Locality gives $r_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m_i$, so the action on $k$ factors through $k_i$. These quotients are fields: if $a$ is outside the maximal ideal, the ideal generated by it and that maximal ideal is the whole ring, which supplies its inverse in the quotient. Apply the two clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], swapping the tensor factors by [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm]. With $(R,J,M,A)=(R_i,\mathfrak m_i,S_i,k)$ and $(R_i,\mathfrak m_i,M_i,k)$ this gives the displayed ring and module identifications for $D_i,P_i$. With $(R,J,M)=(R,\mathfrak m,M)$ it gives $P\cong M/\mathfrak mM$. The ring identification preserves products and units because its formula does so on pure tensors. On $x\otimes[r]$, the composite through $\Psi_i$ is $[r\mu_i(x)]$; hence it is exactly the comparison asserted, independently of the representative $r$.

proof.text: Base change preserves essentially finite type algebras, so k tensor over R_i with S_i is essentially of finite type over the field k. The field is Noetherian; an essentially finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, by the Hilbert basis theorem and preservation under localization. Tensor commutativity transports this property to D_i. The Lean proof uses Algebra.EssFiniteType.isNoetherianRing after its base-change instance.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle paragraph concerning the maps Psi; expanded using Tags 00D2, 00DK, 00FN, 00IK and the directed-colimit equality criterion.

proof.text: If $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ generate $M_i$ over $S_i$, then $x_1\otimes1,\ldots,x_t\otimes1$ generate $P_i$ over $D_i$: write $x=\sum a_tx_t$ and use $x\otimes c=\sum(a_t\otimes c)(x_t\otimes1)$. The map $\Psi_i$ is $D_i$-linear, since $\Psi_i((a\otimes c)(x\otimes e))=s_i(a)\mu_i(x)\otimes ce$. Its kernel is therefore a $D_i$-submodule. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] it is finite.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle paragraph concerning the maps Psi; expanded using Tags 00D2, 00DK, 00FN, 00IK and the directed-colimit equality criterion.

proof.text: Put B = S_i tensor over R_i with R_j, with its right R_j-algebra structure. Tensor commutativity and cancellation of base change give a ring isomorphism beta: B tensor over R_j with k -> D_i, sending (a tensor b) tensor c to a tensor (r_j(b)c). Its restriction theta along B -> B tensor k has the required formula. Apply localization base change to B -> S_j over R_j, obtaining S_j tensor k = D_j as the localization of B tensor k at the image of W_ji. Transport this localization along beta; the composite map from D_i to D_j agrees with d_ji on pure tensors and the image multiplicative subset becomes W_ji.map theta.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle paragraph concerning the maps Psi; expanded using Tags 00D2, 00DK, 00FN, 00IK and the directed-colimit equality criterion.

proof.text: The assumed isomorphism S_j tensor over S_i with M_i -> M_j is S_j-linear: on a pure tensor it sends b tensor x to b times m_ji(x), so linearity follows by tensor induction. Commuting factors and cancelling scalar extensions gives a D_j-linear isomorphism D_j tensor over D_i with P_i -> P_j, sending a tensor x to a times p_ji(x). For the localization of D_i at W_ji.map theta, the universal localized module is also scalar extension to D_j. Compose its canonical scalar-extension isomorphism with the preceding isomorphism. If d_ji(w)b=1, multiplying the image of x/w by d_ji(w) gives p_ji(x), hence the fraction formula is b times p_ji(x). This constructs precisely the required localization equivalence.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle paragraph concerning the maps Psi; expanded using Tags 00D2, 00DK, 00FN, 00IK and the directed-colimit equality criterion.

proof.text: Prove the additive-group colimit property directly. For a compatible family f_i: P_i -> Q, the maps x -> (c -> f_i(x tensor c)) form an additive cocone from M_i into the group of additive maps k -> Q. Descend through the given group colimit M to obtain an additive map M -> (k -> Q). To verify R-balance, represent an element of R and an element of M at stages and pass to a common upper bound. Semilinearity and the tensor balancing relation at that stage prove the balance. The tensor universal property yields a unique additive map M tensor over R with k -> Q with the desired restrictions. Uniqueness follows because each element of M has a stage representative and pure tensors generate. The cocone compatibility is the original M-cocone identity on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle paragraph concerning the maps Psi; expanded using Tags 00D2, 00DK, 00FN, 00IK and the directed-colimit equality criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-localization-system-kernel-stabilization] to the rings $D_i$ with the ring maps $d_{ji}$, the $D_i$-modules $P_i$ with the maps $p_{ji}$, the group $P$ with its compatible $D_i$-actions $(a\otimes c)(x\otimes e)=s_i(a)x\otimes ce$, and the maps $\Psi_i$. Its hypotheses hold: $p_{ji}$ is semilinear over $d_{ji}$ and the transitions obey identities and composition by their formulas; the $D_i$-action on $P$ is the restriction of the $D_j$-action along $d_{ji}$ because $s_js_{ji}=s_i$; each $\Psi_i$ is $D_i$-linear (step 3), $\Psi_jp_{ji}=\Psi_i$ and the $\Psi_i$ exhibit $P$ as the colimit of the underlying abelian groups (step 6); for $i\le j$ the image of $W_{ji}$ in $D_i$ is a multiplicative subset at which $d_{ji}$ localizes (step 4) and $p_{ji}$ is the corresponding module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], so the canonical map $x/w\mapsto d_{ji}(w)^{-1}p_{ji}(x)$ is an isomorphism (step 5); and $\ker\Psi_{i_0}$ is finitely generated over $D_{i_0}$ (step 3). The cited lemma gives $i_1\ge i_0$ with $\Psi_j$ injective for every $j\ge i_1$.
